statements.says: Shared has one door: every folder in Shared names a word from the glossary of the context that claims it.
A folder named in the plural of a glossary headword counts as naming that word.
The glossary grows to cover the plumbing in Shared, rather than the check looking away from it.
Figure, Alphabet, Key, Page, Palette, Wire and Harness become settled glossary words, each with what it beat.
The http folder in Shared is renamed to wire.
The shared-names-a-word check joins the run, so a Shared folder with no glossary word fails dotnet test.
With every Slice check now in the run, the staging hatch that held a rule out of the run is removed.
A new piece of Shared code costs a glossary entry before it costs a folder.
The check knows only three plural endings: a trailing s, ies for y, and es after a hiss.
The second way into Shared, having no domain meaning, was never checked, because whether a piece of code means anything is a judgement.
Running the check over the repository showed the unchecked way was holding fifteen folders, of which only two were plumbing at all.
A plural counts because a folder holds many of a thing.
wire says what the code does, while http says only which protocol it does it over.
Each glossary entry says what the word beat, so the next agent picks the same word rather than inventing a synonym.
The check learns a new plural ending only when a folder needs one, so it stays as small as the tree needs it to be.
Keeping the second door as text was rejected, because a rule half a check can read is a rule an agent reads half of.
Banning plumbing from Shared and giving it a top-level folder of its own was rejected, because it splits the first level between jobs and machinery again and costs more than two glossary entries.

Accepting only an exact headword and renaming every plural folder to the singular was rejected, because those folders read wrong in the singular and a check that makes the tree read worse is a check nobody will keep.
Letting the check accept a settled word found anywhere in the folder name was rejected, because it waves through most names and the door stops being a door.
It supersedes the earlier record that let code into Shared two ways: by naming a glossary word, or by having no domain meaning at all.
